source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The EWS service creates a shared SaveAsListener with retained file/URI/listener state and starts an asynchronous message fetch. Consumers wait for URL stop rather than treating AsyncOpen's return as completion. The listener forwards request status after flush/close, but ignores those final output results, so that status alone does not prove a successful disk flush. The owned test normalizes canonical line endings and compares file bytes after URL stop, with a missing assertion message. Later accepted code uses in-place truncation and removes dummy-envelope support; those are separate phases. No file save or error case ran. The inherited parser buffers incomplete line bytes, while stop has no separate tail write; this is a bounded static limit, not a reproduced data-loss result.
title: EWS save completion comes from the shared stream listener
